resources/what-is-cybersecurity-monitori.title: What is cybersecurity monitoring? A plain‑English guide
resources/what-is-cybersecurity-monitori.description: Cybersecurity monitoring means keeping a continuous, careful watch on what happens in your systems, so unusual activity is noticed early and checked before it becomes a bigger problem.
resources/what-is-cybersecurity-monitori.html:
What does monitoring actually watch?

Every day your systems record activity: people signing in, files being opened or changed, settings being updated, new accounts being created. Most of it is routine. Monitoring looks across that activity for the small number of things that don’t fit, like a sign-in from an unusual location at 2 a.m. or an admin account nobody remembers creating.

Who does the watching?

At CorSentri, AI-enabled technology does the constant watching and flags what looks unusual. Our security team reviews those signals and adds context, such as whether an unusual sign-in is a real concern or a colleague traveling, so you only hear about what matters.

When something needs attention, you get an alert with context: what happened, why it matters and the recommended next step. Alert handling, notification channels and response responsibilities are agreed as part of your service.

Does monitoring make us compliant?

No. Monitoring alone does not make an organization compliant with HIPAA or any other framework. It can support your wider security efforts, for example by helping you review activity in systems that hold sensitive information.

How to get started

Start by listing the systems that hold your most sensitive information. Then talk to a monitoring partner about what they would cover, how alerts reach you and what you can expect in reports.

resources/choosing-a-monitoring-partner.title: What to ask before choosing a monitoring partner
resources/choosing-a-monitoring-partner.description: Choosing a monitoring partner is easier when you know what to ask. These questions show how a provider really works, before you sign anything.
resources/choosing-a-monitoring-partner.html:
What exactly will you monitor?

Ask which of your systems will be covered and which won’t. A good answer is specific, and it explains any limitations up front rather than after something goes wrong.

Who reviews alerts, and when?

Find out whether a person looks at what the technology flags, and whether that happens at night, at weekends and on holidays too. Software alone can produce a lot of noise.

How will you contact us?

Ask who gets notified, through which channels and how quickly. You should be able to choose the contacts, and know what happens if the first person can’t be reached.

What happens after an alert?

Make sure roles are clear. Who investigates, who takes action and who makes decisions? A clear answer here saves confusion when it matters most.

What will reports look like?

Ask to see an example. Reports should tell you what was seen, what it meant and what to improve, in language your team can actually use.

How does onboarding work?

Ask what the provider needs from you, how long setup takes and who does what. A short, clear onboarding plan is a good sign.

What does it cost, and what’s included?

Make sure you know what the price covers and what would cost extra, so there are no surprises later.

Monitoring supports your security program. It doesn’t replace it, and it doesn’t make you compliant on its own. Be wary of any provider that suggests otherwise.

resources/five-warning-signs.title: Five warning signs your systems may need a closer look
resources/five-warning-signs.description: Most security problems don’t start with an obvious break-in. They start with small changes that are easy to miss in a busy week. Here are five worth knowing, and what to do if you see one.
resources/five-warning-signs.html:
1. Sign-ins from unusual places or at unusual times

A colleague who always works from the office suddenly signs in from another country at 3 a.m. It may be travel or a VPN. It may also be someone using a stolen password. Either way, it’s worth a quick check.

2. New admin accounts or changed permissions

An administrator account nobody remembers creating, or a standard user who suddenly has admin rights, is a common sign that someone is trying to keep access to your systems.

3. Repeated failed sign-ins or unexpected password resets

A burst of failed sign-ins on one account, or reset emails nobody asked for, can mean someone is guessing passwords or testing ones taken from another website.

4. New email forwarding rules

A rule that quietly forwards invoices or all incoming mail to an outside address is a classic step in email fraud. It’s easy to set up and easy to overlook.

5. Security tools turned off or activity logs missing

Antivirus disabled on one machine, or a gap in the logs, can be an attempt to hide what’s happening. Large or unusual file downloads at odd hours deserve a look for the same reason.

None of these signs proves an attack on its own. Many turn out to be routine. What matters is that someone notices, checks and decides, quickly.

What to do when you notice one

  • Don’t delete anything. Note what you saw and when.
  • Tell whoever looks after your IT straight away.
  • If an account looks affected, change its password from a device you trust and check its sign-in methods.
  • Check whether the same thing has happened on other accounts.

Why this is hard to do alone

These signs hide among thousands of routine events, and they often appear outside office hours. Monitoring keeps watch across the systems you choose, flags what looks unusual and has a person review it, so the important signals don’t wait until Monday.

cookie-policy.title: Cookie Policy
cookie-policy.description: How the CorSentri website uses cookies, and how to manage your cookie preferences.

sections.title: What cookies are
sections.html:
What cookies are

Cookies are small text files that a website saves in your browser. Similar technologies, such as local storage, work in much the same way. They help a site remember things, such as your settings, and help site owners understand how their pages are used.

This policy explains how CorSentri LLC (“CorSentri”, “we”, “us”) uses them on corsentri.com. It should be read together with our Privacy Policy.

sections.title: Cookies we use
sections.html:
Cookies we use

We group the cookies on this site into two types:

  • Necessary: these keep the website secure and working, such as cookies set by our hosting provider (Webflow), and an entry that remembers your cookie choice. They are always on because the site needs them.
  • Analytics: these help us understand how visitors use the site, such as which pages are viewed and how people move between them. We use Google Analytics and Microsoft Clarity for this. Microsoft Clarity may record how you scroll and click so we can improve the pages. These cookies are off by default and only run if you choose “Accept” or turn them on in Cookie Settings.

When you book a consultation, the booking calendar is provided by Calendly, which may set its own cookies as described in Calendly’s cookie policy.

sections.title: Your choices
sections.html:
Your choices

When you first visit, a banner asks whether you accept analytics cookies. You can accept or reject them, and the site works the same either way.

You can change your mind at any time by opening Cookie Settings, which is also linked in the footer of every page. If you turn analytics off, we stop loading those tools from that point on.

sections.title: Browser settings
sections.html:
Browser settings

Most browsers also let you see, block or delete cookies in their settings. If you block necessary cookies, parts of the site may not work properly. If you clear your browser’s storage, we will ask for your cookie choice again on your next visit.

sections.title: Changes to this policy
sections.html:
Changes to this policy

We may update this policy when we change the tools we use or when the law changes. The “Last updated” date at the top of this page shows when it last changed.

sections.title: Who we are
sections.html:
Who we are

This policy explains how CorSentri LLC (“CorSentri”, “we”, “us”) collects, uses and protects personal information when you visit corsentri.com, fill in one of our forms or book a consultation with us.

CorSentri provides managed cybersecurity monitoring for organizations in the United States. For the purposes of this website, CorSentri is responsible for the personal information described in this policy.

sections.title: Information we collect
sections.html:
Information we collect

We only collect the information we need to respond to you and run this website:

  • Contact details you give us in our contact, partner or risk assessment forms, such as your name, work email, phone number, company name, role and the details you write in your message.
  • Booking details you give when you schedule a consultation through our scheduling tool, such as your name, email address and the time you choose.
  • Technical information sent by your browser, such as your IP address, browser type, device type and the pages you visit. If you allow analytics cookies, this also includes how you use the site.

Please do not send passwords, security credentials or sensitive personal data through our website forms.

sections.title: How we use information
sections.html:
How we use information

We use your information to:

  • Reply to your inquiry and arrange the conversation or consultation you asked for.
  • Prepare and deliver a risk assessment you requested.
  • Discuss our services or a partnership with you, and send information you asked to receive.
  • Keep this website secure, working properly and free from spam or misuse.
  • Understand how the website is used so we can improve it, but only if you have allowed analytics cookies.
  • Meet our legal obligations and protect our legal rights.

We do not sell your personal information, and we do not use it for automated decisions that have legal or similarly significant effects on you.

sections.title: Cookies
sections.html:
Cookies

We use a small number of cookies and similar technologies. Necessary ones keep the site working and remember your cookie choice. Analytics ones help us understand how the site is used, and they only run if you accept them.

You can change your choice at any time through Cookie Settings. Full details are in our Cookie Policy.

sections.title: Sharing information
sections.html:
Sharing information

We share personal information only with service providers that help us run our business. They may use it only to provide their services to us. These include:

  • Our website hosting and form provider (Webflow).
  • Our scheduling provider (Calendly) for consultation bookings.
  • Our email and business software providers.
  • Analytics providers (Google Analytics and Microsoft Clarity), only if you allow analytics cookies.

We may also disclose information when the law requires it, to protect our rights or the safety of others, or as part of a merger, sale or reorganization of our business. Some of our providers may process information outside your state or country. Where they do, we expect them to protect it appropriately.

sections.title: How long we keep it
sections.html:
How long we keep it

We keep personal information only as long as we need it for the purposes in this policy. Inquiry, assessment and booking records are kept while we are in contact with you, and then for as long as we reasonably need them for business records. We review them regularly and delete or anonymize information we no longer need.

If you become a CorSentri client, your information is handled under your service agreement. We may keep some information longer when the law requires it or to resolve disputes.

sections.title: Your choices and rights
sections.html:
Your choices and rights

Depending on where you live, you may have the right to:

  • Ask what personal information we hold about you and get a copy.
  • Ask us to correct or delete it.
  • Opt out of marketing emails at any time, using the unsubscribe link or by contacting us.
  • Withdraw consent to analytics cookies through Cookie Settings.

To make a request, contact us using the details below. We may need to confirm your identity first. We will not treat you differently for using your rights. This website is meant for businesses, and we do not knowingly collect information from children under 13.

We may update this policy from time to time. When we do, we will change the “Last updated” date at the top of this page.
